_schema.platform: Trait Transfer & Genome Editing Intelligence Platform
_schema.principle: Gene identity and literature references are machine-verified against NCBI Gene and PubMed. Portability, linkage drag, pleiotropy and IP remain indicative research signals curated by a breeder, not database facts.

verification_states.verified: Gene ID and at least one reference confirmed in a public database.
verification_states.partial: Gene confirmed, reference not resolved (or the reverse).
verification_states.unverified: Not yet checked, or database returned no match.
verification_states.conflicted: Database answer disagrees with the curated claim — needs human review.

Level 1.label: Commercially Validated
Level 1.desc: Verified in commercial cultivars or released products.

Level 3.label: Genetic Association
Level 3.desc: Supported by QTL, GWAS, linkage mapping, or natural allelic variation.

Level 4.label: Candidate Gene
Level 4.desc: Inferred via orthology, expression profiling, or pathway homology.

Level 5.label: Hypothesis / Research Gap
Level 5.desc: Exploratory polygenic or multi-stress target requiring functional validation.

_schema.level_derivation: A reference counts as confirmed only when PubMed matched the cited author, year and gene, or when a supplied reference resolved by its PMID. A PMID found by topic search alone does NOT count: it may be a different paper about the same gene. Level 1 means this entry's own solution — its mechanism — was commercially applied, not that the trait is on sale by another route. It is never derived: it requires a human to name the product in corrections.json (commercial_product), and the entry records whether the basis is the mechanism being reproduced or the very allele being carried, since the same method on the same gene can yield a different allele. Level 2 — every gene named in the entry resolves in the stated species AND a reference is confirmed. Level 3 — a reference is confirmed but gene identity is incomplete: either only some of the named genes resolve, or none of them do. Level 4 — genes resolve but no reference is confirmed: a candidate by identity only. Level 5 — neither a gene record nor a confirmed reference.

portability_tiers.t1: Native Edit (NGT Cat-1 candidate — crop's own gene/promoter)
portability_tiers.t2: Cisgenic / Introgression (Crossable wild relative — check linkage drag)
portability_tiers.t3: Transgenic / De Novo (Outside primary gene pool)

claims.gene_function: Glutamate decarboxylase; C-terminal autoinhibitory calmodulin-binding domain (CaMBD) regulates GABA synthesis.
claims.evidence_note: Commercially validated (Sicilian Rouge High GABA). 2025 studies across 3 elite backgrounds confirm genotype-dependent vegetative side effects.
claims.scientific_reference: Nonaka et al., 2017 (Sci. Rep.); 2025 Elite Genotype Evaluation
claims.commercial_product: Sicilian Rouge High GABA (Sanatech Seed, Japan, retail since Sept 2021) — the same mechanism as this entry: CRISPR/Cas9 disabling the C-terminal autoinhibitory domain of GAD. The product's own indel is not assumed to be this entry's allele.
claims.patent_reference: Sanatech Seed / Tsukuba Univ. patents (check FTO)
claims.pleiotropic_effects: High GABA levels in certain elite backgrounds can reduce leaf size or fruit weight; cultivar-specific testing required.
claims.conventional_breeding: Limited natural variation in elite lines
claims.editing_possibility: CRISPR-Cas9 premature stop codon in CaMBD

correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13; product claim relayed from Gemini and checked on the web
correction.decision: Set Level 1: the entry's own solution is the commercial product.
correction.rationale: Sanatech Seed's 'Sicilian Rouge High GABA' has been sold to consumers in Japan since September 2021 and is reported as the first commercially sold CRISPR-edited food. The edit is CRISPR/Cas9 on tomato GAD disabling the C-terminal autoinhibitory/calmodulin-binding domain, which is exactly this entry's mechanism, and the fruit carries about 4-6x the GABA of unedited controls. Sources: Nature Biotechnology news (d41587-021-00026-2), Scientific American, and a Philippine regulatory product information sheet naming Sanatech Seed and the GAD target. Recorded as commercial_basis 'mechanism' rather than 'allele': the product was made by the same route on the same gene, but CRISPR repair gives a different indel each time, so claiming the entry's allele is in the fruit would overstate it.

set.commercial_product: Sicilian Rouge High GABA (Sanatech Seed, Japan, retail since Sept 2021) — the same mechanism as this entry: CRISPR/Cas9 disabling the C-terminal autoinhibitory domain of GAD. The product's own indel is not assumed to be this entry's allele.

correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
correction.decision: Keep Sl7-DR2 as the literature symbol and search NCBI under DWF5-2, the symbol it indexes.
correction.rationale: The suggestion's NCBI id LOC101268773 is wrong: that record is 'protein YIP4b-like' on chromosome 7 and has nothing to do with sterols. correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
correction.decision: Search the TOM genes under the older GenBank symbols NCBI indexes: LeTH3/TH3 and LeTH1/TH1.
correction.rationale: Confirmed in NCBI: TH3 (778361, alias LeTH3) is 'tobamovirus multiplication 1 homolog 3' on chromosome 2, and TH1 (778313, alias LeTH1) is 'tobamovirus multiplication 1 homolog' on chromosome 4. Both RefSeq proteins given in the suggestion check out: NP_001234306.1 is homolog 3 and NP_001234096.1 is homolog. The chromosomes agree with the suggested loci (SlTOM1a = Solyc02g080370 on chr2, SlTOM3 = Solyc04g008540 on chr4), which means the NCBI names run opposite to the paper's: the gene the paper calls SlTOM1a is indexed as homolog 3. Anyone editing these must key on the locus tag, not the number in the symbol.
correction.open_question: The draft's second locus, Solyc01g105140, resolves at Sol Genomics to an RNA-binding protein, while the TOM genes resolve as tobamovirus multiplication proteins (Solyc02g080370 and Solyc04g008540, both confirmed). The draft's locus is therefore probably wrong for this entry. Gene identity itself is settled through NCBI TH3/TH1, so this is a stale identifier to remove rather than a gap in the evidence.

entries.trait: Seedlessness (stenospermocarpy) — documented in grape, untested in watermelon

claims.gene_function: D-class MADS-box transcription factor governing ovule integument and seed coat development.
claims.evidence_note: Scientific caveat: Research target ONLY. Has NOT commercially replaced standard triploid seedless watermelon production due to fruit-set/size penalties.
claims.scientific_reference: Wang et al., 2021; Cucurbit AGL11 studies
claims.target_note: Candidate ortholog identified by protein similarity: Cla97C08G144840 on chromosome 8 of the Cla97_v1 build, closest to grape AGL11 and to Arabidopsis STK and clearly separated from the C-class paralogues (see ortholog_candidate for the score profile). On 2026-11-17 a phylogenetic check placed it with the D-class (STK/AGL11) rather than SHP, agreeing with Ensembl Compara's one-to-one call against AtSTK (moderate tree support, 63%). Nothing has been edited or expressed.
claims.pleiotropic_effects: Loss of AGL11 function prevents seed set, which removes the way the line itself is propagated: a seedless diploid cannot be maintained from seed. This is the practical reason commercial watermelon seedlessness runs through triploid hybrids. Any editing route here has to answer how the line is maintained — vegetative or in vitro propagation, a maintainer line, or a conditional allele — before it is a breeding plan rather than a result.
claims.conventional_breeding: Triploid (3x = 2x × 4x) hybrid system remains the commercial standard
claims.recommended_strategy: Genome editing, after the target ortholog is identified
claims.editing_possibility: Native edit candidate: suppress watermelon's own AGL11 ortholog once identified. No specific mutation is defined in this entry, because the ortholog is not identified — so a sequence-based patent search is not yet possible either. The grape evidence is for suppression of the gene, not for a transgene.
claims.gene_action: Loss of function / Tissue-specific promoter edit

correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-16
correction.decision: Restate this as what it actually is: a transfer entry. The solution is documented in grape; watermelon is the target, where it has not been tested.
correction.rationale: The entry claimed ClAGL11 drives diploid seedlessness in watermelon. Nothing supports that: no gene record in Citrullus lanatus, no confirmable citation, and a locus tag from an unreachable build. What is real is the grape work — PMID 26563346 (Ocarez, Plant Cell Rep 2016) reports that suppressing the D-class MADS-box AGL11 gene triggers seedlessness in fleshy fruits — and grape AGL11 resolves in NCBI Gene as MADS5 (100232870). Retiring the entry would throw that away; an external review recommended retiring it because it read the question as whether watermelon itself was validated. A documented solution with an untested target is not a defect here, it is the point. The claim shrinks and becomes true: AGL11 suppression causes seedlessness in fleshy fruits, and nobody has tried it in watermelon.

superseded.why: ClAGL11 as a watermelon gene is unsupported and is replaced by the grape source gene. The locus tag belongs to the 97103 v2 build, which is unreachable, and is dropped. ClWIP1 is a different trait and moved to its own entry, WAT-SEX-01.

correction.open_question: Next steps are now concrete, in this order: confirm Cla97C08G144840 is the AGL11 ortholog with a phylogenetic tree over the conserved domains and ovule expression; then, with a real sequence in hand, a sequence-based patent search becomes possible for the first time. The IP position remains an unverified lead until someone supplies patent publication numbers — see ip_signal.

ip_signal.status: lead now grounded in real patent numbers, but it is not the patent that was supplied
ip_signal.supplied_claim: An external AI named EP3046410A1 (said family: WO2015036378A1, US20160222401A1) as the concrete patent covering seedlessness via AGL11 loss of function in Cucurbitaceae.
ip_signal.checked: 2026-11-16, via web search of the patent family and the applicant's own trait-patent page
what_is_true: The family is real: 'Plants with an intense fruit phenotype', Nunhems B.V., priority 2013-09-18.

It does carry a Cucurbitaceae-level aspect: a plant whose endogenous AGL11-like ortholog has reduced amount, activity or function, the ortholog being of the tomato TAGL11-like protein of SEQ ID NO: 3.
Species-specific aspects are sequence-bound: Cucumis sativus against SEQ ID NO: 12, Cucumis melo against SEQ ID NO: 22, each at 75% cDNA identity or more.
what_is_wrong: EP3046410A1 is withdrawn (EP14766735.6, 'not_active Withdrawn'), so it is not a live European right to clear.
The WO number is WO2015040098, not WO2015036378. The applicant's own trait-patent page lists WO2015040098 with US10212898 B2 and US11202420 B2.

The trait is not seedlessness. The intense phenotype is a flesh-texture trait: in tomato the homozygous intense alleles turn the locular gel in the seed cavities into fleshy tissue. The specification extends the orthologs to fruit texture and fruit tissue characteristics, not to seed suppression.
No watermelon sequence was found among the species-specific aspects retrieved; Citrullus is reached only through the family-level Cucurbitaceae wording.

more_relevant_find.why: A watermelon-specific right over a flesh-texture phenotype that also provides the gene and markers for identifying it in Citrullus lanatus. For a watermelon AGL11 question this is closer to the point than the withdrawn EP.

ortholog_candidate.how_it_was_found: scripts/find_ortholog.py aligned the grape gene and its close relatives against the whole Citrullus lanatus Cla97_v1 proteome (22,541 proteins). The paralogues were included as queries on purpose, because a best match means little if a paralogue scores almost as well.
ortholog_candidate.why_this_one: It is closest to both D-class queries and about 165 points clear of the nearest C-class paralogue, which is the discrimination that matters here. The runner-up by score, Cla97C01G024020 (718 against VviAGL11, 696 against AtSHP2), turned out in the tree to belong to the C-class AGAMOUS lineage. An 8.2 kb multi-exon span also fits a MADS-box gene.
ortholog_candidate.what_this_is_not: Not proof of function. Subfamily membership is now supported by two independent lines (Ensembl Compara one-to-one call and our own tree, see phylogeny_check), so this is the watermelon AGL11/STK orthologue on present evidence. Whether it acts in the ovule, and whether suppressing it gives seedless fruit in watermelon, is untested; expression in the ovule would be the next biological check.
ortholog_candidate.contradicts: Both chromosome-7 identifiers previously attached to this entry. The draft's own tag Cla97C07G144940 exists in no reachable build. The locus suggested by an external analysis, Cla97C07G140950, does exist but carries no annotation, spans only 722 bp, and does not appear among the top candidates here. The best candidate is on chromosome 8.

phylogeny_check.verdict: groups with the D-class (STK/AGL11), not with SHP
phylogeny_check.summary: Two independent lines agree. (1) Ensembl Compara's own gene tree calls Cla97C08G144840 a one-to-one ortholog of Arabidopsis STK (AT4G09960) and of grape Vitis18g02617. (2) Our tree over the MADS, I and K regions places it in the clade with Arabidopsis STK, tomato AGL11 and grape AGL11; in 0 of 200 bootstrap trees did it group with SHP1/SHP2, while SHP1+SHP2 held together in 196 of 200. Like the other D-class proteins it has no N-terminal extension before the MADS domain; AG, SHP1, SHP2 and TAGL1 all have one. Identity over that region: 88.3% to grape AGL11, 81.9% to AtSTK, 74.3–74.9% to SHP1/SHP2.
phylogeny_check.also_found: Cla97C01G024020, earlier listed as the D-class runner-up, groups instead with the C-class AGAMOUS lineage (with Cla97C03G058570 in 151/200 trees, next to tomato AGAMOUS). Cla97C02G044160 sits with tomato TAGL1 (PLENA/SHP lineage), weakly (67/200).
phylogeny_check.limits: 63% bootstrap is moderate support, not strong. 13 sequences, one alignment, one model; no other cucurbit sequence (the cucumber orthologue came back as a 114 aa fragment). This settles which subfamily the gene belongs to; it does not show that the gene acts in the watermelon ovule or that suppressing it gives seedless fruit. Files: data/phylogeny/WAT-SEED-01/.

locus_claims_checked.checked: 2026-11-16 against the Citrullus lanatus Cla97_v1 proteome from Ensembl Plants (22,541 proteins)

Cla97C07G144940.detail: No protein carries this tag, and chr7 tags in this build stop around Cla97C07G1445xx, so the number is outside the chr7 range.
Cla97C07G144940.supplied_as: the watermelon AGL11 locus, said to belong to the Cla97 v2/v2.5 annotation
Cla97C07G144940.note: In Ensembl Plants the Cla97C-style identifiers come with assembly name Cla97_v1, which does not match the claim that this style is the v2/v2.5 naming. Not checkable against CuGenDB from here.

Cla97C07G140950.reading: Too short for a MADS-box gene, which typically carries several exons over a few kb. Existing is not the same as fitting.

Cla97C08G144840.reading: The span fits a MADS-box gene, and this is the protein-similarity candidate. Still a candidate, not an established ortholog.

set.trait: Seedlessness (stenospermocarpy) — documented in grape, untested in watermelon
set.target_note: Candidate ortholog identified by protein similarity: Cla97C08G144840 on chromosome 8 of the Cla97_v1 build, closest to grape AGL11 and to Arabidopsis STK and clearly separated from the C-class paralogues (see ortholog_candidate for the score profile). On 2026-11-17 a phylogenetic check placed it with the D-class (STK/AGL11) rather than SHP, agreeing with Ensembl Compara's one-to-one call against AtSTK (moderate tree support, 63%). Nothing has been edited or expressed.
set.editing_possibility: Native edit candidate: suppress watermelon's own AGL11 ortholog once identified. No specific mutation is defined in this entry, because the ortholog is not identified — so a sequence-based patent search is not yet possible either. The grape evidence is for suppression of the gene, not for a transgene.
set.recommended_strategy: Genome editing, after the target ortholog is identified
set.pleiotropic_effects: Loss of AGL11 function prevents seed set, which removes the way the line itself is propagated: a seedless diploid cannot be maintained from seed. This is the practical reason commercial watermelon seedlessness runs through triploid hybrids. Any editing route here has to answer how the line is maintained — vegetative or in vitro propagation, a maintainer line, or a conditional allele — before it is a breeding plan rather than a result.

claims.patent_reference: Beijing Academy of Agriculture & Forestry Sciences

claims.gene_action: Gain of function (ClTST2) / Loss of function (ClLCYB for red flesh)

correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
correction.decision: Narrow this entry to ClTST2 and move ClSWEET3 and ClLCYB out of it.
correction.rationale: PMID 29118248 (Plant Physiol 2018, first author Ren Y, 'A Tonoplast Sugar Transporter Underlies a Sugar Accumulation QTL in Watermelon') characterises ClTST2 and its upstream regulator, not ClSWEET3 or ClLCYB — so the draft bundled three genes under one paper that covers one of them. Flesh colour (ClLCYB) is a different trait from sugar accumulation and should never have shared an entry with it. Two corrections to the suggestion: the accession it gave for ClTST2, MF497324, is a Marquandomyces marquandii fungal ITS sequence, not watermelon; the real record is KY367352.1, /gene=TST2, product 'tonoplast sugar transporter 2', protein ATQ36703.1. And Citrullus lanatus does have NCBI Gene records (185 of them), though none is named TST, SWEET or LCYB, so the practical conclusion stands: identity has to come from GenBank.

superseded.why: Not characterised in PMID 29118248. ClSWEET3 needs its own entry and its own paper; ClLCYB is flesh colour, a separate trait. Removed here rather than left implying evidence they do not have.

correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-14
correction.decision: Point the three PPO genes at the eggplant V4 annotation, and drop the draft's locus.
correction.rationale: Sol Genomics hosts the eggplant V4 annotation with functional descriptions, and its V3-to-V4 table converts the V3 tags that were supplied: SMEL_008g312490/500/510 map to SMEL4_08g009050/060/070. All three are annotated 'Similar to Polyphenol oxidase B, chloroplastic' and sit adjacent on chromosome 8 between 12.139 and 12.156 Mb — the tandem PPO cluster the entry is about. The GenBank accessions supplied alongside those tags were wrong organisms entirely, so the tags turned out to be the useful part of that suggestion.
correction.open_question: Which of the three adjacent PPO genes is PPO4, PPO5 and PPO6 is NOT established here. The cluster is confirmed and all three members are polyphenol oxidases, but the symbol-to-locus assignment within it comes from the supplied V3 list, not from the paper. Read PMID 33343607 before relying on a specific one. Separately, the draft's own locus SMEL4.1_08g017350 is wrong for this entry: SMEL4_08g017350 is annotated as a U11/U12 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein, on chromosome 8 at 54.4 Mb, far from the PPO cluster.

claims.gene_function: LONELY GUY (LOG) family cytokinin biosynthetic enzyme; expressed mainly in immature prickles.
claims.evidence_note: Scientific distinction: SmMYB candidates are under investigation; should NOT be presented as a single-gene proven CRISPR solution.
claims.scientific_reference: Miyatake et al., 2020; Solanaceae prickle genetics
claims.linkage_drag: Classical prickle-free donors sometimes carry calyx size differences.
claims.pleiotropic_effects: Trichome/prickle pathways can overlap with insect deterrence.
claims.editing_possibility: Promoter editing, or marker-assisted selection on the CAPS marker at -735 bp: the causal variation reported is non-coding, so a coding knockout is not the route the natural prickleless allele uses.
claims.trait_inheritance: Single dominant nuclear gene (PE locus, chromosome 6)

correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13
correction.decision: Replace the draft's SmMYB candidates with SmLOG1 as the gene, keeping SmMYB recorded as a superseded candidate.
correction.rationale: PMID 38974191 fine-mapped the PE locus on chromosome 6 to a 9233 bp interval holding one candidate, SmLOG1, a LONELY GUY family cytokinin biosynthetic enzyme, and CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of it abolished prickles in all tissues. The draft's SmMYB candidates are a different gene and that paper does not support them.

superseded.why: Not supported by PMID 38974191. Kept here so the earlier hypothesis is not silently erased; if another source supports an SmMYB role, it can return as its own entry.

correction.second_suggestion_note: A later suggestion attributed PMID 38974191 to 'Satterlee et al., 2024, Science'. That is wrong and contradicts the same supplier's earlier, correct attribution: the paper is Zhang L, Horticulture Research 2024. It also offered the locus tag SMEL4.1_06g011220.1.01, which cannot be checked here because eggplant has no NCBI build.
correction.journals_from: external AI suggestion (Gemini), 2026-11-13; unverified until a match lands
correction.open_question: The locus resolves in the eggplant V4 annotation on chromosome 6, which is where PMID 38974191 fine-mapped the PE locus — so the position agrees. But V4 annotates it 'Protein of unknown function', so the annotation does NOT corroborate a LONELY GUY cytokinin enzyme. Identity here is positional, not functional: the paper is the only source for what the gene does.

max_level.why: Identity here is positional only. The locus exists on chromosome 6, where the paper mapped the PE locus, but the V4 annotation calls it 'Protein of unknown function', so nothing independent confirms it is a LONELY GUY cytokinin enzyme — and the symbol-to-locus assignment came from an external suggestion, not from the paper. Level 2 would claim functional validation of a gene whose identity rests on agreement of chromosome number.

correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
correction.decision: Narrow the entry to CRa, anchored to GenBank AB751517.
correction.rationale: PMID 23054353 is confirmed: Ueno H, Plant Mol Biol 2012, 'Molecular characterization of the CRa gene conferring clubroot resistance', and AB751517.1 is confirmed as Brassica rapa subsp. pekinensis CRa mRNA for a putative disease resistance protein. The paper covers CRa only, so CRb, Crr1 and Crr3 do not belong in this entry. The suggestion's NCBI gene ID 103860516 is not usable: that record is 'uncharacterized LOC103860516', not the TMV-resistance-like protein described, so identity comes from the accession instead.

superseded.why: Not characterised in PMID 23054353. The PMIDs offered for them were checked and are wrong papers entirely: 23175754 is about cellulose microfibrils in collenchyma, and 24831572 is a cardiovascular medicine review. Each locus needs its own entry and a real reference.

correction.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1. The literature does document that CR loci have been introduced into commercial F1 cultivars of Chinese cabbage, and that CRb/CRbKato is the same allele as CRa (Breeding Science 72:21040; Hatakeyama et al. 2017), and Syngenta holds a patent on monogenic dominant clubroot resistance introgressed into B. oleracea. But the specific cultivar names offered — Kilaton F1, Clapton F1, Crispus F1, Monclano F1 — could not be tied to CRa by any source found, and 'carries a major CR locus' is not the same claim as 'carries this gene'. Needs one source naming a cultivar and its locus.

correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13; product claim relayed from Gemini and checked on the web
correction.decision: Set Level 1: the commercialised hybrids carry the allele this entry names.
correction.rationale: Traka et al., New Phytologist 2013 (doi 10.1111/nph.12232) reports that two high-glucoraphanin F1 hybrids were commercialised as Beneforte broccoli and that all of them carry an introgressed Brassica villosa segment containing a B. villosa Myb28 allele, with 2.5-3x the glucoraphanin of standard hybrids. The product and the entry's gene are the same thing. Note this is an introgression from a crossable wild relative, so the route is cisgenic, not a native edit. Recorded as commercial_basis 'allele', unlike the tomato entry: this is an introgression, which moves the actual B. villosa Myb28 allele into the hybrid rather than creating a new variant, so the product does carry the allele this entry names.

ortholog_candidate.method: protein similarity against the Brassica oleracea proteome, with MYB28/29/34 all as queries
ortholog_candidate.score_profile: Bo9g175680 1357 to AtMYB29; Bo7g098110 1193 to AtMYB34; no top hit was closest to AtMYB28
ortholog_candidate.reading: R2R3-MYB proteins in this clade are too similar for this method to separate reliably, and the absence of any MYB28-closest hit is itself the warning sign. Treat these as 'a MYB of this clade', not as the named gene.
ortholog_candidate.to_confirm: a MYB-family tree over the R2R3 domain plus the published Brassica MYB28/29 nomenclature
ortholog_candidate.note: HAG1 was removed from the wanted list: it is a synonym of MYB28, which this entry already resolves in NCBI Gene. The draft wrote 'MYB28 (HAG1)' and the symbol parser made two genes of one.

claims.gene_function: Lachrymatory factor synthase (AcLFS) converts 1-propenyl sulfenic acid into tear-inducing propanethial S-oxide.
claims.evidence_note: Commercially validated (tearless onions), but NOT a simple single-gene knockout due to multi-copy LFS genes and sulfur pathway interactions.

claims.linkage_drag: Low-pungency often correlates with shorter storage dormancy; requires careful multi-trait selection.

claims.environmental_interaction: Soil sulfur availability strongly affects pungency

claims.editing_possibility: CRISPR-Cas9 / RNAi (challenging due to large ~16 Gb genome & multi-copy LFS)

correction.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
correction.decision: Narrow the entry to LFS, anchored to GenBank AB089203.
correction.rationale: AB089203.1 is confirmed as Allium cepa lfs mRNA for lachrymatory factor synthase, and Allium cepa has no NCBI Gene build, so the accession is the identity anchor. PMID 18583530 silences LFS by RNAi; it does not test AcACS1 or AcACS2, so those leave this entry.

superseded.why: Not tested in PMID 18583530. Onion pungency via ACS genes is a separate trait needing its own entry and reference.

correction.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1, and this is the clearest case of why the rule matters. Sunions is a real marketed tearless onion from BASF/Nunhems, but BASF states it is the result of more than three decades of CONVENTIONAL breeding, with pungency tracked by pyruvic acid measurement. This entry's solution is RNAi silencing of LFS (PMID 18583530). Same trait, different genetic route: the product does not validate the entry's solution, so Level 1 would be a false claim.
